data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":["SCR_003","SRC_008"],"disanalogies":["In statistics, the true model is a theoretical object; in evaluation, it is an empirical generative process that may be partially observable.","Statistical identifiability is a population property; the evaluation question is about a single finite sample, where identifiability may fail even if it holds in population.","The proxy may introduce its own bias (if the proxy is correlated with the checklist cues), confounding the bias estimate."],"overturn_conditions":["If a proxy is successfully constructed and panel errors correlate with it, the decomposition is instantiated and the claim is testable.","If the checklist is provably complete (covers all outcome-relevant features), no proxy is needed and the panel dominates unconditionally."],"shared_structure":["Both require access to the true model (or a proxy) to decompose error into bias and variance.","Both identify the construction of diagnostic items (proxy-divergent or out-of-distribution) as the practical bottleneck.","Both conclude that without such items, the evaluation is inconclusive about the mechanism."],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_003","SCR_002","SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["The reduction to proxy existence transfers: the evaluation is only informative if proxy-divergent items can be constructed.","The inconclusiveness result transfers: without proxies, no within-evidence distinguishes the mechanisms."]},"claim":"The bias-variance decomposition is the covering principle, but it cannot be empirically instantiated in a single evaluation without a proxy for the true generative model; therefore the question reduces to whether proxy-divergent items can be constructed, and if not, no within-evidence can distinguish genuine gain from compliance.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the true generative model is known or directly accessible (atypical case), no proxy is needed and the decomposition is direct.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If proxy features exist but are not outcome-relevant, they cannot reveal bias.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist encodes all observable outcome-relevant features, no proxy-divergent items can be constructed, but this also means the checklist is complete and the panel dominates unconditionally.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The bias-variance frame requires separating bias (systematic deviation from truth) from variance (noise). In a single evaluation, this requires knowing the true generative model to compute bias. Without it, observed accuracy confounds bias and variance. A proxy for the generative model can be constructed from outcome-relevant features that the checklist does not encode: if panel errors correlate with these features, bias is revealed. But if no such proxy features exist (either because the checklist is complete or because the omitted features are not observable), the decomposition cannot be performed, and the evaluation cannot distinguish genuine understanding from compliance. The question thus reduces to the existence of constructable proxy-divergent items.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
